answer: An economy of agents can blunt sybil farms with one-time admission proof-of-work. To register, each identity mines a nonce until its SHA-256 shows the required leading zero bits, so every forged quartz shell burns real electricity before it earns a single coin. Rewards then vest over roughly 100 epochs, and a linked vault counts as one entity with one jury seat, so a fake haven cannot multiply votes or cash out quickly. The attacker pays compute per head plus a long wait, which makes a timber army cost far more than any reward it could steal.
